FST 2004.title: Exploring Food Science Careers
FST 2004.description: Food science specialization areas and career opportunities. Experiential learning opportunities developed through bridge experience platform. Introduction to research, internship, study abroad and individualized learning. Career preparation, job and internship search strategies.

FST 2014.title: Introduction to Food Science
FST 2014.description: Fundamentals for food science and technology. Integration of basic principles of food safety, human nutrition, food spoilage, and sensory evaluation with the appropriate technology of food preservation and processing.

FST 2024.title: From Raw to Burnt: Exploring Science and Society through Foods
FST 2024.description: Food as a method of studying scientific principles and development of society, including acquiring, preserving, processing and consuming foods. Integration of chemistry, biology and physics of grains; salt and spices; meat, poultry, and fish; dairy and eggs; fruits and vegetables; and fat and oils, with the advancements in and the cost to human civilization from historical and ethical perspectives of food production. Scientific principles demonstrated in food preparation.

FST 2044.title: Food, War and Conflict
FST 2044.description: Explores historical developments in food preservation, processing and distribution relative to the commencement or continuation of conflict. Examines why and how wars have been fought over economic policies, food trade, and control of food supplies. Examines food defense efforts to protect food and water from intentional contamination and acts of terrorism and bioterrorism. Focus on food products and the preservation, processing and distribution technologies that arose from, or enabled, war and conflict.

FST 2244.title: Topics in Food Science and Technology
FST 2244.description: Variable topics in food science and technology such as emerging trends, challenges and regulatory policy. Qualitatively and quantitatively explore relevant and timely issues facing food systems. May be repeated for a maximum of six credits with different topics. Pre: Sophomore standing.

FST 2424.title: Introduction to Food and Beverage Fermentation
FST 2424.description: Principles, processes, and applications of fermentation in the context of food and beverage production. Explores various fermentation techniques, the chemical processes and microbiology involved, and the role of fermentation in enhancing flavor, texture, preservation, and nutritional value. Hands-on experience through workshops and sensory evaluation.

FST 2544.title: Functional Foods for Health
FST 2544.description: Introduction to functional foods (foods with additional value beyond basic nutrition) including development of functional foods, novel sources, and traditional foods with value-added health benefit; regulatory issues; and media messages.

FST 3024.title: Principles of Sensory Evaluation
FST 3024.description: Principles of sensory evaluation including theory, sensory physiology and psychology, experimental methods, applications, and statistical analysis.

FST 3114.title: Wines and Vines
FST 3114.description: Development of a working knowledge of world wine styles, wine appreciation, and sensory evaluation of wine. Emphasis on the influences of grape growing and winemaking practices on wine quality, style, economic value, and significance in global food culture. Pre: Must be at least 21 years of age.

FST 3124.title: Brewing Science and Technology
FST 3124.description: Study of chemical reactions important in brewing of beer and hard cider. Effects of variations in malting, mashing, and other processing steps on characteristics and quality of beer; fruit sugar, acid and fermentation impacts on cider composition and quality. Investigation of reactions that cause flavor deterioration.

FST 3214.title: Principles of Meat Science
FST 3214.description: Muscle biology and biochemistry, fresh meat processing, meat merchandising, processed meats, food safety, meat cookery, and regulations.

FST 3324.title: Food Processing and Engineering I
FST 3324.description: Basic principles of unit operations. Heat and mass transfer. Equipment in commercially important food processing applications. Source and variability of raw food materials. Raw food materials and packaging. Processing methods to ensure food safety and quality. Raw agricultural material conversion to a given food product
FST 3324.prereq: BIOL 2604 and (MATH 1025 or MATH 1524 or MATH 1225)

FST 3514.title: Food Analysis
FST 3514.description: Data analysis, sampling techniques, theory and practice of chemical and physical methods of food analysis for determination of food composition; application of analytical methods of quality control and food laws and regulations.

FST 3604.title: Food Microbiology
FST 3604.description: Examination of the role of microbes (bacteria, fungi, viruses and parasites) in food safety and quality and strategies for facilitating their control. Understanding microbes used in food production, including fermented foods and beverages.

FST 3614.title: Food Microbiology Lab
FST 3614.description: Methods to quantify, identify, and characterize spoilage, pathogenic, and pathogenic microbes in foods and food processing environments. Comparison of classical and rapid detection methods to characterize and identify microbes in food. Characterization of effects of food processing methods on microbes in food.

FST 3900.title: Bridge Experience
FST 3900.description: Application of academic knowledge and skills to in a work-based experience aligned with post-graduation goals using research-based learning processes. Satisfactory completion of work-based experience often in the form of internship, undergraduate research, co-op, or study abroad; self-evaluation; reflection; and showcase of learning. Pre: Departmental approval of 3900 plan.

FST 4004.title: Food Science Experiential Learning Reflection
FST 4004.description: Reflection of skills and knowledge developed during food science experiential learning process. Analyze curriculum. Development of communication skills to reflect and evaluate their experience.

FST 4014.title: Concepts of Food Product Development
FST 4014.description: Application to the food industry of principles and standard practices of research and product development; functionality of food ingredients; students will work in teams to design and develop a new food product.

FST 4104.title: Applied Brewing Science and Engineering
FST 4104.description: Chemistry, biochemistry, and engineering aspects of brewing operations in the production of beer. Barley, malting, hops, brewing operations, fermentation chemistry, yeast characteristics and finishing operations examined. Calculations of raw materials, brewing and fermentation schedules, and final specifications conducted. Laboratory exercises focused on brewing, brewery engineering, and analysis of intermediate and final products.

FST 4204.title: Advanced Topics in Food Science and Technology
FST 4204.description: Variable advanced topics in food science and technology such as emerging trends, challenges and regulatory policy. Qualitative and quantitative exploration of relevant and timely issues facing food systems. May be repeated for a maximum of six credits with different topics. Pre: Junior standing.

FST 4304.title: Food Processing
FST 4304.description: Basic principles of unit operations. Heat and mass transfer. Equipment in commercially important food processing applications. Raw food materials and packaging. Processing methods to ensure food safety and quality.
FST 4304.prereq: BIOL 2604 and BIOL 2614 and (MATH 1025 or MATH 1524)

FST 4314.title: Food Processing Laboratory
FST 4314.description: Safety and good manufacturing practice of food processing. Operation of key equipment found in the food industry. Collection, analysis and interpretation of data acquired in lab exercises. Documentation and reporting of findings.

FST 4324.title: Food Processing and Engineering II
FST 4324.description: Advanced principles of food engineering, including unsteady heat and mass transfer, rheology, and process design, and their application in current thermal and mechanical processing technologies, such as extrusion and microwave heating. Emerging food processing technologies such as high-pressure processing, cold plasma, and membrane separation. Sustainability in food processing through waste management, packaging, and process optimization. Simulation and automation tools to enhance food system efficiency.

FST 4504.title: Food Chemistry
FST 4504.description: Overview of the chemical and functional properties of food components including major (water, proteins, carbohydrates, enzymes and lipids) and minor (vitamins, minerals, flavors, pigments) constituents; chemical, biochemical reactions and physical phenomena occuring during food handling, processing, and storage; their impact on the nutritional and sensorial quality of food.

FST 4524.title: Food Safety and Quality Assurance
FST 4524.description: Monitoring safety and quality of food as well as compliance with government regulations. Description of regulatory agencies and food regulations. Development of specifications, food standards and safety critical control points. Systems to assure a safe and quality product, including acceptance sampling and statistical process control.

FST 4534.title: Food Chemistry Lab
FST 4534.description: Investigation of functional properties of proteins, carbohydrates, and lipids in processed foods including effect of environmental conditions; solubility, foaming ability and textural properties of proteins, carbohydrate crystallization, ability of polysaccharides to form gels and pastes, lipid absorption and tenderization, characterization of a natural-occurring enzyme.

FST 4544.title: Distillation and Fermentation Analysis
FST 4544.description: Sampling and analysis of pre-and post-fermentation foods and beverages to determine process termination, efficiency, and formation of desired and non-desired products. Laws and regulations pertaining to fermented foods and beverages. Distillation as an analytical tool and as a production method for food/beverage products.

FST 4634.title: Epidemiology Foodborne Disease
FST 4634.description: Overview of causes, transmission, and epidemiology of major environmental, food, and water borne diseases. Outbreak and sporadic detection, source tracking and control of pathogens. Overview of the impact of foodborne outbreaks on regulatory activities at the national and international level. Corequisite: Enrollment in either FST 3604 or BIOL 4674.

FST 4644.title: Fermentation Microbiology
FST 4644.description: Physiology, biochemistry, and genetics of microorganisms used for production of food ingredients, fermented foods, and beverages. How microorganisms are used in fermentation and the effects of processing and manufacturing conditions on production of fermented foods.

FST 4654.title: Food and Beverage Fermentation
FST 4654.description: Introduction to the broad range of fermented foods and beverages. Defining quality parameters of fermented foods and beverages. In-depth examination of the processing methods and equipment employed in commercial-scale production of fermented foods and beverages. Historical, cultural, sensory, and nutritional attributes of fermented foods and beverages. Course requirements may be satisfied by taking FST 3604 or FST 4504 prior to or concurrent with course.

FST 5004.title: Graduate Seminar
FST 5004.description: Special topics, critical reviews, and discussions of current literature throughout a wide range of subject areas in food science and technology. May be repeated.

FST 5014.title: Sensory Evaluation of Food
FST 5014.description: Principles of sensory evaluation including experimental methods, applications, and statistical analyses.

FST 5034.title: Good Agricultural and Manufacturing Practices
FST 5034.description: Principles of food safety management for food producing and food processing environments. Emphasis on guidelines developed in Good Agricultural Practices for plant-based foods and Current Good Manufacturing Practices. Pre: Academic and/or professional background in food processing, quality assurance, fresh produce production, food product regulation, and/or food safety. Graduate standing required.

FST 5044.title: Global Food Laws and Regulations
FST 5044.description: History of laws and regulations that affect the food processing industry and food consumers. Impact of legal and regulatory issues on food quality, safety, formulation, labeling, marketing, grading, product and process development, and international trade for the U.S. and other nations. Pre: Academic and/or professional background in food processing, quality assurance, and/or food safety.

FST 5054.title: Professionalism in Food Scienc
FST 5054.description: Applied principles and skills in communication, research ethics and research project design for the food science profession. Pre: Graduate standing. P/F only.

FST 5094.title: Grant Writing and Ethics
FST 5094.description: A framework for writing clear, concise grant proposals in a team-oriented, multidisciplinary approach from concept development through submission to a funding agency. Potential ethical dilemmas that may arise in academic, industrial, or federal research settings will be discussed. PRE: Undergraduate courses in one of the following: organic chemistry (CHEM 2565/2566), cell & molecular biology (BIOL 2104), Concepts of Biochemistry (BCHM 2024), or equivalent. Graduate standing required.

FST 5604.title: Advances in Food Microbiology
FST 5604.description: Critical review of current topics in food microbiology. Foodborne pathogens, toxins, analytical methodology, food spoilage, inhibition and destruction of bacteria, standards, and fermentations.

FST 5614.title: Food Safety and Security
FST 5614.description: Identification and prevention of food safety and security hazards that may result in intentional or unintentional contamination. Development and implementation of plans to enhance food safety and security in the processing, distribution, transportation, and retail segments of the food supply chain. Pre: Academic and/or professional background in food processing, quality assurance, and/or food safety. Graduate standing required.

FST 5624.title: Applied Food Microbiology and Sanitation
FST 5624.description: Overview of the causes, transmission, and epidemiology of major environmental, food-, and water-borne diseases in the food industry. Detection, monitoring, and control of important environmental pathogens. Chemical, physical, and biological sanitation to control pathogens in food, water, and the environment. Pre: Academic and/or professional background in microbiology, food safety, or environmental health. Graduate standing required.

FST 5634.title: Epidemiology of Food and Waterborne Diseases
FST 5634.description: Causes, transmission, and epidemiology of major environmental, food, and waterborne diseases. Outbreak and sporadic detection, surveillance, source tracking, and control of pathogens. Impact of food-borne outbreaks on economy and regulatory activities at the national and global level. Risk assessment and strategies for prevention across diverse agricultural scales. Pre: Graduate standing.

FST 5664.title: Flavor Chemistry
FST 5664.description: Study of flavor compounds, their isolation, extraction, and flavor profiles. Examination of compounds that are used to produce commercial flavors from synthetic and natural sources. Graduate standing required.

FST 5734.title: Data Analytics for Food and Agricultural Sciences
FST 5734.description: Computer programming for food and agriculture research. Data analysis for research projects in food and agricultural sciences. Writing scripts for data wrangling (importing, cleaning, organizing) and coding for research (data exploration and inference). Data visualization for exploratory and expository data analysis and inference using programmatic approaches in R. Pre: Graduate Standing.
